event.summary: Old terminals and their running work end on upgrade (specification-accepted; proposed drop)
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Updating a supervisor ends programs still running in old terminals and discards their terminal screen and scrollback. Details: The assigned deletion removes the old control-client replay/output path (parent stream.rs lines 1–1205 in the assigned packet). SPEC.md at the reviewed commit, Terminal experience, lines 3003–3016 expressly changes the product contract: 'This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' The original uses a straight apostrophe in host's. The same paragraph explicitly says an ended agent's 'terminal’s last screen, which lived in the server, is gone; old tabs are closed' (straight apostrophe in original), and 'A session whose agent or tabs already run in terminal hosts keeps them.' Suggested bucket: highest (loss of running user-owned processes/work); could-be-highest: yes, the specified upgrade path directly ends running programs. Confidence: confirmed specification acceptance, source-only; startup implementation still to be checked for the claimed boundaries. proposed_drop: specification acceptance only, requiring independent check; exact ASCII source text is: 'This release ends them: the first time a host's supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveats: this record does not allege an unauthorized implementation deviation; the charter requires potentially highest issues accepted solely by specification to remain findings proposed for drop. The implementation must still preserve terminal-host sessions, and that check continues.

event.summary: Deleting the replay stream does not remove replay or pane isolation for surviving host terminals
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether removing tmux replay, pane filtering, query stripping and guarded output-client ownership would corrupt a surviving terminal or stop its work. Details: Source search at the reviewed commit finds no remaining uses of open_replay_stream, ReplayStreamCandidate, request_pause or resume_paused_with_replay in supervisor source; the sole OutputStream hit is an obsolete comment at service/connection.rs:986. service/core.rs:6675–6704 separates old rows (no terminal lookup) from adopted HostTerminal runtimes. service/handlers.rs:1688–1716 resolves a HostTerminal, refuses bytes-only clients before takeover, and :1928–1966 installs GridSender with that terminal's own input pump, notice subscription and shutdown/pause channels. hosts/terminal.rs module contracts :1–83 describe the independent per-host connection/emulator, journal replay and terminal-query handling; the commit's full patch to hosts/terminal.rs does not remove its journal feeding or query handling. SPEC_impl.md, Terminal host, :1963–1980, :2108–2168 and :2624–2671 establish the replacement journal/emulator/grid contracts. Assigned stream.rs mechanisms are specific to old tmux control clients, which no surviving terminal uses. Suggested bucket: other for the ruled-out implementation concern; could-be-highest: yes if deletion had made a viewer block another terminal's work or contaminate input/output, but no such shipped route is established and the independent host path refutes dependence on the deleted mechanism. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of this deletion concern, not a complete review of the independent host implementation. proposed_drop: source refutation (no dependent runtime caller and separate host/grid implementation). possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveats: intentional destruction of old terminals remains separately recorded as f1; source-only analysis, no observed execution.

event.summary: No distinct test-sensitivity defect established from retiring tmux stream tests
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Considered whether retiring the stream's tests removes checks for output/history loss or unsafe teardown that surviving host terminals still need. Details: The assigned patch packet (old stream.rs lines 1–1205) contains production code, not the test module; additional context search locates the old test module at parent :1709 onwards. Inspected parent :2632–2710: the abandoned-candidate test gates tmux no-output acknowledgement, verifies the exact control client remains before acknowledgement, then is reaped, and confirms the private tmux server survives. Those are assertions about the deleted per-attachment tmux control client, not a host lifecycle guard that production retained. Host attachments create no such client (handlers.rs:1928–1966), and GridStream catches up from the independent existing emulator (:414–497). Separately inspected the surviving tests' actual assertions, not just production: grid_stream/tests.rs:313–333 checks message ordering and exact numbered history; :338–379 establishes catch-up remains unfinished before injecting more output, then checks exact uninterrupted history after quieting; :485–506 waits for processed flood plus an observed parked sender before asserting no paused output, and exact history/no reset after resume; :520–546 establishes a full writer queue before draining and asserting exact history/no reset. These source-level assertions distinguish the relevant replay/pause/queue loss mechanisms. They are not claimed as an equivalent test for tmux's retired server-abort protocol, nor proof of complete host test coverage. Suggested bucket: other (considered test-sensitivity gap, not an established production defect). could-be-highest: no established catastrophic tooling consequence; potential user work/history corruption from deleting production mechanisms remains explicitly preserved in c2, with its original wording. Confidence: source-confirmed refutation of needing the old no-output/candidate test for the retained implementation; no distinct surviving responsibility was found lost in this assigned deletion. proposed_drop: source/test-assertion analysis, pending independent check. possible_cover: none; coverage/queue sources not searched. Caveats: no test execution or mutation experiment, no claim that correct production alone proves test sensitivity, and no comprehensive review of neighbouring groups' test deletions. This is a considered candidate, not a new implementation finding.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: A maintainer tracing terminal-output loss is told to consult a first diagnostic checkpoint in a stream implementation this commit deletes. Details: connection.rs:985–987 says 'Output-path checkpoint; see the first one in `OutputStream::next_output`. Data frames only: control replies are not what that path loses.' Assigned stream.rs deletion includes the OutputStream type and its control-client ownership; the same complete file deletion removes next_output in the adjacent assigned batch. At this revision an allowed-source git grep for the deleted type/method/cutover names finds this single residual reference and no executable caller. This is a concrete stale present-tense diagnostic map, distinct from the source-refuted runtime dependency in c2 (which already noted this residual but did not validate it as a documentation defect). Suggested bucket: other/documentation correctness if attribution is confirmed. could-be-highest: no, no security or loss-of-work consequence established for the pointer. Confidence: source-confirmed missing target; historical validity and later repair still to check. proposed_drop: false pending those checks; not a finding of bad runtime logging or loss of data. possible_cover: none in the fully read interface snapshot. Missing readily checkable premise: confirm the referenced first checkpoint exists before deletion and whether a later in-range patch repairs this instruction. No runtime tests or reproduction. Scope caveat: caller reference is examined only as an implication of assigned stream deletion, not a separate review of the connection writer.
